I found 8 defects on `feature/batch-import`, and 7 of them reproduce when run. The worst: `notes search` on the command line now crashes, and `replace_all` can delete notes it never replaces. All 7 existing tests still pass at head, and none of them cover these failures.

**What I compared:** branch head `936eb89` against `main` (`54c2c91`, which is also the merge-base). The working tree was clean, so this is a commit-to-commit review. I read all five changed files plus the unchanged modules that use them (`cli.py`, `links.py`, `sync.py`). Nothing was excluded.

**How I tested:** `python3 -B .scratch/batch-import-bugs/probes.py <checkout>`, run once on the head checkout and once in a temporary worktree at base. The output is in `head.log` and `base.log`. A second script, `dup_stems.py`, repeats the duplicate-filename import 50 times (`dup_stems.log`). All of these are in `.scratch/batch-import-bugs/`, which git ignores. Your checkout is unchanged.

## Defects

1. **`notes search` on the command line crashes** (`notes/index.py:20-26`, which breaks `notes/cli.py:13`)
   - **Trigger:** `python -m notes.cli search <word>` when at least one note matches.
   - **Consequence:** `index.search` now returns `(note_id, score)` pairs, but `cli.py` still joins the results as strings. The command fails with `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, tuple found`. At base the same call returns `(0, 'weekly-plan')`.
   - **Origin:** new; a regression in code the branch didn't touch. The test was changed to expect the new tuples, but no test runs `cli search`.
   - **Evidence:** executed.
   - **Impact:** search no longer works for command-line users whenever there is a match.

2. **`replace_all` deletes every note before it knows the import will succeed** (`notes/batch.py:24-26`)
   - **Trigger:** any file in the source folder that can't be read: not valid UTF-8, no permission, or two files with the same name (defect 3).
   - **Consequence:** with an existing note "Keep Me", importing a folder holding `good.md` and a non-UTF-8 `bad.md` raised `UnicodeDecodeError`. Afterwards the store held only `['good']`, so "Keep Me" was gone. The error does reach the caller, but the deleted notes can't be recovered.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** executed.
   - **Impact:** permanent loss of the user's notes. Import into a staging folder and swap it in, or delete only after every file has been read.

3. **Files with the same name in different subfolders make `import_dir` fail or overwrite each other** (`notes/batch.py:10,17`, together with the shared `.tmp` path at `store.py:19`)
   - **Trigger:** the import searches subfolders, and the note id comes from the file name alone. So `2024/plan.md` and `2025/plan.md` both become id `plan`. All workers then write to the same `plan.tmp`.
   - **Consequence:** with 8 `plan.md` files, all 50 runs raised `FileNotFoundError: .../plan.tmp -> .../plan.md`. Some files are written before the error. Even without the parallel workers, all but one file would be lost without any error.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** executed (50 out of 50 runs).
   - **Impact:** a common folder layout (one folder per year or project) can't be imported. Combined with defect 2, this also deletes the old notes.

4. **Searches and `export_search` still return deleted notes** (`notes/index.py:9-14`; exposed by `store.delete` and `batch.replace_all`)
   - **Trigger:** search, delete a note (or run `replace_all`), then search again in the same process.
   - **Consequence:** the in-memory index only adds and updates entries; it never drops deleted ones. After `replace_all`, `export_search("parser")` returned 2 and wrote `['old-parser', 'plan']`, while the store held only `['plan']`. The same stale entry existed at base, but base had no delete feature that would reach it.
   - **Origin:** made worse. The branch's new test `setUp` clears the index before each test, which hides this.
   - **Evidence:** executed.
   - **Impact:** exported lists include ids that no longer exist, and loading them fails with `FileNotFoundError`.

5. **Imported notes keep the raw file name as their id instead of the usual slug** (`notes/batch.py:17`)
   - **Trigger:** importing `Weekly Plan.md`.
   - **Consequence:** the note's id becomes `Weekly Plan`, although `store.py:1` says notes are "named by the slug of their title". The link pattern in `links.py:6` only accepts `[a-z0-9-]`, so no note can ever link to it. An imported `[[weekly-plan]]` link points at a note that doesn't exist.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** executed. The ids came out as `['Retro', 'Weekly Plan']`, and `backlinks("Weekly Plan")` returned `[]`.
   - **Impact:** links between imported notes break. Likely fix: `note_id=store.slug(path.stem)`.

6. **The sync key change makes other team members' clients see every note twice** (`notes/sync.py:23`)
   - **Trigger:** running `push` against a bucket that clients on `main` have already pushed to.
   - **Consequence:** the old `notes/<id>.md` keys stay in the bucket and new `notes/v2/<id>.md` keys are added. The `sync.py` docstring says other team members' clients "treat every key as a note", so each note shows up twice for them. The probe ended with `['notes/retro.md', 'notes/v2/retro.md']`.
   - **Origin:** new. The test was loosened from an exact `assertEqual` on all keys to `assertIn`, which no longer catches this.
   - **Evidence:** executed against the in-memory test remote (`FakeRemote`). I did not test the production S3-style bucket (`RemoteStore`).
   - **Impact:** you decide; see question 1.

7. **`average_words` crashes on a folder with no `.md` files** (`notes/batch.py:33`)
   - **Trigger:** an empty source folder, or one without Markdown files.
   - **Consequence:** `ZeroDivisionError`.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** executed.
   - **Impact:** any caller has to guard this case itself. Returning 0 or `None` would avoid it.

8. **The new search treats multi-word queries as "any of these words"** (`notes/index.py:20-25`)
   - **Trigger:** `search("ship parser")`.
   - **Consequence:** it matches notes containing either word. Before, multi-word queries matched nothing.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** inferred from reading the code; not run.
   - **Impact:** this looks like the intended ranking feature, so it is listed only for completeness and may need no action.

## Outside the change
None found.

## Questions for the author
1. Was moving the sync keys to `notes/v2/` meant to be a migration? If so, where do the old `notes/` keys get removed, and how do clients still on `main` avoid showing duplicates?
2. Should `import_dir` keep subfolder names in the id (for example `2024-plan`), or reject duplicate names before writing anything?

## Minor observations
- `import_dir` updates the shared index from 4 worker threads at once. In the current code that is safe, because each update only adds dictionary entries. If something else calls `search` on another thread at the same time, it could fail with "dictionary changed size during iteration". No such caller exists in this repo, so I didn't test it.

**Not covered:** the real S3 remote, case-insensitive filesystems (where `Plan.md` and `plan.md` would collide), and running the tests under a coverage tool.

1. **`replace_all` deletes every note before the import has succeeded** (`notes/batch.py:24-26`)
   - **Trigger:** the source path is mistyped or missing, the source has no `.md` files, or any file in it fails to import (non-UTF-8 text, a permission error, or the duplicate-name race in item 3).
   - **Consequence:** the user's notes are deleted from disk with no backup. When the source is missing, the call reports success and returns `[]`.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed.
     - `replace-missing-source` → `replace_all(typo dir) -> []`, `ids after: []`
     - `replace-bad-file` → raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, and `ids after: ['good']`: the old note is gone and only part of the new set was imported.
   - **Impact:** the user loses their data. Importing into a staging location first and deleting only after it succeeds would prevent it.

2. **The CLI `search` command now crashes** (`notes/index.py:26`, used by `notes/cli.py:13`)
   - **Trigger:** `python -m notes.cli search <term>` whenever anything matches.
   - **Consequence:** `search()` now returns `(id, score)` pairs, but the CLI still passes the result straight to `", ".join(...)`. The command fails with `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, tuple found`.
   - **Origin:** new. The CLI file did not change; the function it calls did.
   - **Evidence:** executed (`cli-search`). The base prints `weekly-plan` and exits 0. The head raises the `TypeError`.
   - **Impact:** every CLI search that finds a note fails. No test covers the CLI search path.

3. **Two source files with the same name in different subfolders race and lose a note** (`notes/batch.py:10-17`, `store.py:19-21`)
   - **Trigger:** `import_dir` searches subfolders too (`rglob`), so `2024/plan.md` and `2025/plan.md` both get the id `plan`. They are imported in parallel and both write to the same temporary file, `plan.tmp`.
   - **Consequence:** the result is random. In 20 runs:
     - 12 raised `FileNotFoundError: 'plan.tmp' -> 'plan.md'` after one copy had already been written.
     - 8 returned `['plan', 'plan']` with no error, keeping whichever copy finished last ("new" 6 times, "old" 2 times).
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (`duplicate-stems`, repeated 20 times).
   - **Impact:** one note is lost without warning. Through `replace_all`, the error also triggers item 1.

4. **Sync now pushes to `notes/v2/` instead of `notes/`, and the test was relaxed to allow it** (`notes/sync.py:23`)
   - **Trigger:** any `push` to the shared bucket.
   - **Consequence:**
     - The key change itself is executed: the base pushes `notes/weekly-plan.md`, the head pushes `notes/v2/weekly-plan.md`.
     - The effect on other users is inferred from the module docstring (lines 4-5), which says teammates' clients "treat every key as a note". The predicted result: notes already in the bucket under `notes/` stay there and stop being updated, and every note pushed from now on appears a second time under `notes/v2/`.
   - **Supporting signal:** `weakened_checks.py` flags that the exact-keys assertion was replaced by `assertIn("notes/v2/retro.md", ...)`. That check would no longer catch duplicate or stale keys.
   - **Origin:** new. The commit message does not mention it.
   - **Settling check:** pull from a bucket that has keys under both `notes/` and `notes/v2/` using the current client.
   - **Action:** you decide; see the first question below.

5. **Search results and `export_search` still include deleted notes** (`notes/index.py:9-14`, exposed by `store.delete` and `batch.export_search`)
   - **Trigger:** search once (which fills the in-memory index), then `delete` or `replace_all`, then search again.
   - **Consequence:** the index adds and updates entries but never removes them. After `replace_all`, `search('parser')` still returns `retro` and `weekly-plan`, `export_search` writes both ids and returns 2, and `export_note('retro')` then returns `False`.
   - **Origin:** made worse. The index behaved this way before, but this branch adds the first in-library ways to delete notes.
   - **Evidence:** executed (`stale-index`). The new test `setUp` clears `index._cache` before each test, so no test sees this.
   - **Impact:** an export lists notes that no longer exist.

6. **Imported notes use the raw file name, not the slug** (`notes/batch.py:17`)
   - **Trigger:** importing a file such as `Weekly Plan.md`.
   - **Consequence:** the note gets the id `Weekly Plan`. The README says notes are named by title slug, and `[[...]]` links only match `[a-z0-9-]`. So `[[weekly-plan]]` does not resolve (`load('weekly-plan')` raises `FileNotFoundError`), and nothing can link to the imported note. A later `store.save("Weekly Plan", ...)` creates a second note, `weekly-plan`.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (`unslugged-id`).

7. **`average_words` on an empty folder raises `ZeroDivisionError`** (`notes/batch.py:33`)
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (`average-empty`).
   - **Impact:** a loud crash, low severity. The caller has to guard against an empty folder.

## Minor observations

- `_import_one` rebuilds the whole index after every file it imports (`batch.py:18`), so an import does work proportional to files × notes. This only matters for large note sets, which I did not measure.

- Should duplicate file names across subfolders be rejected, or turned into distinct ids?

final:
I reviewed branch `feature/batch-import` at `936eb89` against its merge-base with `main`, `54c2c91`. That covers the 5 changed files plus the code that uses them. The working tree was clean, and nothing was generated, binary or excluded. I found 9 defects. The worst one: `notes search` on the command line now crashes on any search that finds something. The existing 7 tests pass, but none of them catches these.

To reproduce, run `python3 -I .scratch/batch-import/probe.py <checkout>` (Python 3.14.8) against the branch and against the base commit, which I checked out temporarily and then removed. The output is saved in `.scratch/batch-import/head.log` and `base.log`, and the race traceback in `race.log`. The checkout is unchanged.

## Defects

1. **`notes search` crashes on any match.** `notes/index.py:26` and `notes/cli.py:13`
   - **Trigger:** `python -m notes.cli search <term>` where at least one note contains the term.
   - **Consequence:** `search()` now returns `(note_id, score)` pairs, but the command line still joins the results as plain strings. It fails with `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, tuple found`. On `main` the same input prints `weekly-plan` and exits 0.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** I ran it on both revisions.
   - **Impact:** search from the command line no longer works. Neither the command line nor any other caller of `search()` was updated, and no test covers `cli search`.

2. **`replace_all` deletes every note before it imports anything.** `notes/batch.py:24-26`
   - **Trigger:** any import failure, such as a `.md` file that isn't valid UTF-8, the same-name race in item 3, or a missing source folder.
   - **Consequence:** the exception propagates and the store is left empty or only partly filled. I ran it with one undecodable file: it raised `UnicodeDecodeError` and the store went from `['keep-me']` to `[]`.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** I ran it.
   - **Impact:** notes are permanently lost, with no way to roll back.

3. **Importing two files with the same name at once crashes the import.** `notes/batch.py:17`, with the temporary-file write at `notes/store.py:19-21`
   - **Trigger:** `import_dir` on a folder tree where two subfolders contain a file with the same name, such as `a/todo.md` and `b/todo.md`. The search goes into subfolders, so this is easy to hit.
   - **Consequence:**
     - The 4 worker threads write the same temporary file, `todo.tmp`. One thread renames it into place, and the next rename fails with `FileNotFoundError: '…/todo.tmp' -> '…/todo.md'`. This happened in all 200 of 200 runs with 8 identical names.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** I ran it.
   - **Impact:** the import aborts part-way. When this happens inside `replace_all`, it combines with item 2 and the existing notes are lost.

4. **Files with the same name silently overwrite each other.** `notes/batch.py:17`
   - **Trigger:** the same folder layout as item 3, but without the crash.
   - **Consequence:** `import_dir` returned `['todo', 'todo']`, but the store holds a single note. Which file's text survives depends on thread timing; in my run it was `'from a'`.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** I ran it.
   - **Impact:** the caller is told 2 notes were imported, but 1 was lost without any error.

5. **Deleted notes still show up in search and exports.** `notes/store.py:29-30` and `notes/batch.py:24-25`, against the cache in `notes/index.py:9-14`
   - **Trigger:** `store.delete` or `replace_all`, followed by `search` or `export_search`. `refresh()` only adds or updates cache entries and never removes them.
   - **Consequence:** `search("parser")` still returns `('weekly-plan', 1)` after that note is deleted. After `replace_all`, `export_search` wrote `old\nplan` and returned 2, although the store holds only `['plan']`.
   - **Origin:** made worse. The cache never removed entries on `main` either, but this change adds the delete functions that expose it.
   - **Evidence:** I ran it. The test setup now clears `index._cache`, which hides this from the tests.
   - **Impact:** exported files list notes that don't exist, and `export_note` then skips them.

6. **Pushed notes move to a new remote location that team members' clients don't read.** `notes/sync.py:23`
   - **Trigger:** any `push` after this change.
   - **Consequence:** keys move from `notes/<id>.md` to `notes/v2/<id>.md`. According to the comment at `notes/sync.py:3-5`, other team members' clients pull the same bucket and "treat every key as a note". Depending on how those clients map keys to notes, either they get a second copy of every note, or newly pushed edits never replace the old ones. The old keys are never removed.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** inferred. I didn't have the other clients' code. To settle it, have an old-format client pull from a bucket that holds both `notes/x.md` and `notes/v2/x.md`.
   - **Impact:** what team members see goes out of sync. The test was loosened from an exact `assertEqual` to `assertIn` (`tests/test_notes.py:23`), so a stale or duplicated set of keys would still pass.

7. **Imported notes keep their file names instead of the usual ID format.** `notes/batch.py:17`
   - **Trigger:** importing a file whose name isn't already in that format, such as `Weekly Plan.md`. Normally note IDs come from the title, lower-cased with dashes (the slug, e.g. `weekly-plan`).
   - **Consequence:** the note gets the ID `Weekly Plan`. Saving a note titled "Weekly Plan" then creates a second note, giving `['Weekly Plan', 'weekly-plan']`. The `[[link]]` pattern (`notes/links.py:6`) only matches IDs made of `[a-z0-9-]`, so other notes can't link to the imported one.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** I ran it.
   - **Impact:** duplicate notes, and imported notes that can't be linked.

8. **`average_words` crashes on an empty folder.** `notes/batch.py:33`
   - **Trigger:** a folder with no `.md` files.
   - **Consequence:** `ZeroDivisionError`.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** I ran it.
   - **Impact:** callers have to guard against an empty folder themselves.

9. **Import time grows with the square of the store size.** `notes/batch.py:18`
   - **Trigger:** every imported file triggers `index.refresh()`, which checks the modification time of every note in the store.
   - **Consequence:** file-status calls grew from 1,286 for 50 files to 20,140 for 200 files, so 4× the files cost about 16× the calls. A 10,000-note import would make on the order of 50 million calls.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** I ran it, counting calls to `os.stat`.
   - **Impact:** large imports slow down sharply. The refresh is also unnecessary there, because `search()` already refreshes.

## Questions for the author

- Was the `notes/v2/` key change meant to come with a migration, or a reader change in the other clients? Your answer decides whether item 6 is fixed by reverting the key or by shipping a migration alongside it.
- Should `import_dir` turn file names into the usual ID format, and reject or rename files with the same name? Items 4 and 7 depend on that choice.

## Gaps

- I didn't test the real remote store or other team members' clients; item 6 is reasoned from the code and comments.
- I didn't measure test coverage or run a linter or type checker; this review is from reading the code plus the probes.
